text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- Poland's Finance Minister Marek Belka is planning to privatise Poland's family jewels, the most successful firms. Belka told the paper in an interview he expected parliament to pass bill reforming the social security system this year. The finance ministry will not press on the central bank to cut interest rates, Belka said.
- Salmed '97 medical products exhibition and Domexpo '97 consumer goods exhibition will start on March 18 on the site of Poznan international fair in western Poland.
- The Senate's plan to tax income of the state forests watchdog would jeopardise many environmental programmes the institution is running, the state forests' official said.
- Poland may join the EU between 2000 and 2006, a recent report by the London-based Royal Institute for International Affairs said.
- Austria's Creditanstalt is officially bidding to buy Polski Bank Inwestycyjny (PBI) bank. Poland's Kredyt Bank and the U.S.'s GE Capital are also interested in the purchase.
- Four companies are ready to invest $50 million in the special economic zone planned in the city of Lodz in central Poland, Lodz provincial governor Andrzej Peczak said.
- Poland is ready for direct mailing marketing because there is too much traditional advertising in the media, Ammurati Puris Lintas marketing director Coleen Cahill said.
- Polfa Kutno pharmaceutics maker's 1997 net profit will reach 21 million zlotys, a forecast by the Bank Handlowy Capital Operations' Centre (BH COK) said.

- The Malopolski Browar Strzelec brewery share capital will grow by up to 8.2 million zlotys following a new C-series share issue and public trading of the A-series and B-series shares, the company extraordianry shareholders meeting decided.

- Only strong capital groups will survive competition on Poland's meat processing market, Sokolow meet processing firm's president Krzysztof Lewczuk said. The firm has taken over the Kolo meat plant and is planning to acquire Ostroleka meat processing firm.
- Grey and Corporate Profiles/DDB advertising agencies have received the lion's share of the prestigious DEA Awards in the 1997 issue of the competition.

- Construction works at the Gliwice-based General Motors car plant have been under way for the last two months. The first batch of Opel cars made in Gliwice will leave the factory in September 1998, GM Poland spokesperson Zbigniew Lazar said.
